nodes.name: NF cleaning and Hydrothermal NiV hydroxide
nodes.procedure: First, Ni foam (NF, 2 × 3 cm) was cleaned with 4.0 M HCl and deionized water for 15 min in an ultrasonic bath. The NiV/NF was synthesized by a hydrothermal method. In brief, the desired amount of NiCl₂·6H₂O, VCl₃·6H₂O, urea (9 mmol), and NH₄F (4 mmol) were dissolved in deionized water (40 mL). The total amount of metal ions was kept at 3 mmol, different molar ratios of Ni:V were used to prepare Ni₁₋ₓVₓ/NF (x = 0, 0.08, 0.25, and 0.5). Afterward, the above solution was transferred into a 50 mL Teflon-lined autoclave and heated at 120°C for 12 h. The as-prepared samples were washed by deionized water and dried at 60°C for 10 h.

nodes.name: Phosphidation to V-Ni₂P/NF
nodes.procedure: The as-prepared Ni₁₋ₓVₓ/NF and NaH₂PO₂ powder (400 mg) were placed at two separate crucibles with NaH₂PO₂ on the upstream side of the tube furnace. The samples were annealed at 350°C for 2 h with a ramping rate of 3°C min⁻¹ under Ar atmosphere.
nodes.source_text: Preparation of Vₓ-Ni₂P/NF Electrodes: The as-prepared Ni₁₋ₓVₓ/NF and NaH₂PO₂ powder... under Ar atmosphere.

nodes.name: In situ electrochemical reconstruction
nodes.procedure: The obtained electrodes were reconstructed in situ by using cyclic voltammetry (CV). The Vₓ-Ni₂P/NF electrodes were cycled in 1.0 M KOH solution from -0.1 to 0.7 V versus saturated calomel electrode (SCE) for 3000 cycles at a scan rate of 50 mV s⁻¹.
nodes.source_text: Preparation of Vₓ-Ni₂P/NF-AC Electrodes: The obtained electrodes were reconstructed... at a scan rate of 50 mV s⁻¹.

properties.description: High-resolution image showing nanostructured material with circular features

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM suggests nanosheet morphology for V-Ni₂P/NF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The transmission electron microscopy (TEM) suggests a nanosheet morphology for V-Ni₂P/NF (Figure 1c).

nodes.characterization_summary: HR-TEM displays interplanar spacing of 2.02 Å corresponding to the (201) plane of Ni₂P for V-Ni₂P/NF; post-activation shows disordered structure with 2.34 Å (011) plane of Ni oxyhydroxide.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution TEM (HR-TEM) image displays an interplanar spacing of 2.02 Å, corresponding to the (201) plane of Ni₂P (Figure 1d).

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS elemental mapping indicates homogeneous distribution of Ni, V, and P; post-activation shows decreased P and V intensities with increased O.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The energy dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) elemental mapping indicates the homogeneous distribution of Ni, V, and P elements throughout the nanosheet.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD of V-Ni₂P/NF indexed to hexagonal Ni₂P with suppressed peaks and shift to higher angles; post-activation shows disappearance of Ni₂P peaks.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The X-ray diffraction (XRD) pattern of V-Ni₂P/NF can be well indexed to hexagonal Ni₂P (ICDD: 00-03-0953).

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS Ni 2p_{3/2} at 852.9 eV for V-Ni₂P/NF with 0.4 eV negative shift vs Ni₂P/NF; V 2p shows V^{3+}, V^{4+}, V^{5+}; post-activation Ni-O at 856 eV, new O 1s peaks at 529.3 and 531.2 eV.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray photoelectron spectra (XPS) of Ni2p_{3/2} for V-Ni₂P/NF show the main peak at 852.9 eV, confirming the formation of metal phosphide.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP shows V content decreases from 11.9 to 0.51 wt% and P from 22.6 to 0.33 wt% after activation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: ICP analysis... where the V and P contents decrease from 11.9 to 0.51 w/w% and 22.6 to 0.33 w/w%, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman of V-Ni₂P/NF-AC shows Ni-O vibrations at 475 and 555 cm^{-1}; intensity ratio B/A = 0.82 indicating increased β-NiOOH phase.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The corresponding Raman spectrum of V-Ni₂P/NF-AC displays two characteristic peaks at 475 and 555 cm^{-1}, corresponding to the Ni-O vibration of Ni oxyhydroxide.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni K-edge XANES of V-Ni₂P/NF-AC shows adsorption edge shift to high energy indicating increased Ni oxidation state; remaining V shifts edge to lower energy vs Ni₂P/NF-AC.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ni K-edge XANES spectra of V-Ni₂P/NF-AC display a shift of adsorption edge toward high energy after electrochemical oxidation.

nodes.characterization_summary: EXAFS shows broadening of Ni-O and Ni-M peaks for V-Ni₂P/NF-AC indicating disordered structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The first two peaks in the Fourier transforms (FTs) of EXAFS are well fit by Ni-O and Ni-M correlations, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: CV in non-Faradaic region at different scan rates gives double-layer capacitance C_dl = 7.14 mF cm^{-2} for V-Ni₂P/NF-AC, higher than pre-catalyst.
nodes.evidence_snippet: A C_dl value of 7.14 mF cm^{-2} is obtained for V-NiP/NF-AC, higher than 5.47 mF cm^{-2} attained for the V-NiP/NF pre-catalyst.
